Upper respiratory tract infections for example, sinusitis and pharyngitis.

items.t: H. pylori eradication (duodenal ulcer), triple therapy for 6 to 14 days: clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily with lansoprazole 30 mg twice daily plus amoxicillin 1000 mg twice daily or metronidazole 400 mg twice daily; or with omeprazole 40 mg daily plus amoxicillin 1000 mg twice daily or metronidazole 400 mg twice daily; or with omeprazole 20 mg daily plus amoxicillin 1000 mg twice daily.

src.q: Eradication of H. pylori in patients with duodenal ulcers (Adults) The usual duration of treatment is 6 to 14 days.

Triple Therapy Clarithromycin (500mg) twice daily and omeprazole 40mg daily should be given with amoxycillin 1000mg twice daily or metronidazole 400mg twice daily.
Triple Therapy Clarithromycin (500mg) twice daily and omeprazole 20mg daily should be given with amoxycillin 1000mg twice daily.

items.t: Prolonged-release: one 500 mg tablet once daily with food; severe infections two 500 mg tablets once daily; usual duration 6 to 14 days.

src.q: The usual recommended dosage of Xetinin XL Tablets in adults is one 500mg modified-release tablet daily to be taken with food. In more severe infections, the dosage can be increased to two 500mg modified-release tablets daily. The usual duration of treatment is 6 to 14 days.

items.t: Hepatic dysfunction (raised enzymes, hepatocellular/cholestatic hepatitis, fatal hepatic failure) reported. Caution in impaired hepatic function. Patients should stop and contact their doctor if anorexia, jaundice, dark urine, pruritus or tender abdomen develop.

Patients should be advised to stop treatment and contact their doctor if signs and symptoms of hepatic disease develop, such as anorexia, jaundice, dark urine, pruritus, or tender abdomen.

items.t: Caution in moderate to severe renal impairment.

src.q: CDAD has been reported to occur over two months after the administration of antibacterial agents
Drugs inhibiting peristalsis should be avoided.

items.t: Pneumonia: sensitivity testing important (macrolide-resistant S. pneumoniae); in hospital-acquired pneumonia combine with other antibiotics. Skin infections: test sensitivity.

src.q: it is important that sensitivity testing be performed when prescribing clarithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia
In hospital-acquired pneumonia, clarithromycin should be used in combination with additional appropriate antibiotics.

src.q: This should be taken into account in patients with diabetes mellitus.
Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicinal product.
This may be harmful for people with phenylketonuria.

items.t: Prolonged-release tablets contain lactose: patients with galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take them.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

If clarithromycin is essential to use, simvastatin must be stopped whilst the patient is taking the course of clarithromycin.

items.t: Atorvastatin: SmPC advises caution with other statins (lowest dose, monitor for myopathy). SPS: avoid and use a non-interacting antibiotic if possible; consider pausing atorvastatin for the course; if unavoidable use a maximum of 20 mg daily. src.q: Caution should be exercised when prescribing clarithromycin with statins.

items.t: Warfarin: risk of serious haemorrhage and marked INR rise; monitor INR and prothrombin time frequently. Caution with DOACs (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban, edoxaban), especially if high bleeding risk.

src.q: There is a risk of serious haemorrhage and significant elevations in International Normalized Ratio (INR) and prothrombin time when clarithromycin is co-administered with warfarin
INR and prothrombin times should be frequently monitored while patients are receiving clarithromycin and oral anticoagulants concurrently.

items.t: Oral hypoglycaemic agents (e.g. sulfonylureas) and/or insulin: significant hypoglycaemia possible; monitor glucose carefully.

src.q: The concomitant use of clarithromycin and oral hypoglycaemic agents (such as sulfonylurias) and/or insulin can result in significant hypoglycaemia. Careful monitoring of glucose is recommended

items.t: Calcium-channel blockers metabolised by CYP3A4 (e.g. amlodipine, verapamil, diltiazem): caution, risk of hypotension; levels of both may rise.

src.q: Caution is advised regarding the concomitant administration of clarithromycin and calcium channel blockers metabolized by CYP3A4 (e.g., verapamil, amlodipine, diltiazem) due to the risk of hypotension.

items.t: Sildenafil (and tadalafil, vardenafil): increased exposure; consider dose reduction.

src.q: Reduction of sildenafil, tadalafil and vardenafil dosages should be considered when these drugs are co-administered with clarithromycin.

items.t: Hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine: carefully weigh benefits and risks (increased cardiovascular events and mortality seen with azithromycin + hydroxychloroquine); use with caution, especially with cardiac risk factors.

src.q: careful consideration should be given to the balance of benefits and risks before prescribing clarithromycin for any patients taking hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine
if there is a clinical need to prescribe systemic macrolide antibiotics with hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine, use caution in patients with risk factors for cardiac events

src.q: Caution should be exercised in concomitant use of clarithromycin with systemic and inhaled corticosteroids that are primarily metabolised by CYP3A

items.t: Suspension (children): creatinine clearance < 30 ml/min/1.73 m2 - halve to 7.5 mg/kg per day; not beyond 14 days.

src.q: In children with creatinine clearance less than 30 ml/min/1.73 m2, the dosage of clarithromycin should be reduced by half to 7.5 mg/kg per day. Dosage should not be continued beyond 14 days in these patients.
